purpose: Operational finite representations for the unchanged NEX-1 v0.1 self-hosting path, reconciling accepted functional streams with the complete Stage 5.11 representation inventory.

decision.reason: v0.3 supplies exact operational carriers, canonical token grammars, equality/canonicality rules, failure-layer separation, bounded examples, and a machine validator without changing NEX-1 v0.1

BitStream.rule: for a finite bit string of length L, stream(i) is its 0/1 bit for i<L and EOF for every i>=L

FiniteBits.canonical_rule: length is exact; stream(i) is 0/1 for i<length and 2 for every i>=length
FiniteBits.equality: same length and same stream(i) for every i<length; EOF behavior is required after length

NatTokenStream.rule: for a finite token sequence of length L, token(i) is the i-th natural token for i<L and 0 for every i>=L

FiniteNatTokens.canonical_rule: length is exact; token values at indices 0..length-1 are the complete canonical token sequence; out-of-range values are ignored and canonically 0
FiniteNatTokens.equality: same length and same token(i) for every i<length

Bits.canonical_rule: every finite bit string has one extensional FiniteBits value

Term.canonical_rule: exactly one complete token tree consumes the entire sequence
Term.child_addressing: children are located by token cursor and structural skip; no recursive Core type is assumed
Term.wire_relation: decodeTerm must transform canonical NEX wire Bits into Term tokens; encodeTerm must reconstruct canonical NEX wire from Term tokens and may not return or copy an opaque original wire value

Type.canonical_rule: exactly one complete type token tree consumes the entire sequence

Scheme.canonical_rule: bound IDs are unique and strictly ascending; portable normalized schemes alpha-rename bound IDs to 0..k-1

Substitution.canonical_rule: typeVarId keys are unique and strictly ascending

TypeEnvironment.canonical_rule: nearest binder first; exact binding count

PortableObservation.canonical_rule: exactly one complete observation consumes the sequence; Function remains the coarse portable top-level observation

ToolResult.payload_rule: Ok payload is operation-specific canonical tokens; failure payload is a versioned portable detail token sequence

runtime_state_policy.status: no additional first-class runtime state required by Stage 5.11
runtime_state_policy.reason: a substitution-based Stage 5.15 evaluator may operate directly on Term tokens; Stage 5.11 therefore does not assume a hidden closure/environment object
runtime_state_policy.future_rule: if Stage 5.15 requires additional finite evaluator state, a new meta-representation version must freeze its exact FiniteNatTokens grammar before that state is used

canonicality: Canonicality is semantic/extensional for function-valued streams; closure syntax or host identity is never compared.
FiniteBits has an exact length and EOF at every index at or beyond that length.
FiniteNatTokens has an exact length and an exact token sequence.
Term tokens are a complete canonical prefix serialization of exactly one NEX term tree.
Type tokens are a complete canonical prefix serialization of exactly one type tree.
Scheme bound IDs and substitution keys obey their normalization/order rules.
Malformed internal token representation is distinct from malformed canonical NEX wire.
Invalid de Bruijn scope and unknown primitive ID are not wire-codec errors; they remain Stage 5.13 structural validation outcomes.
Resource refusal is not serialized as semantic invalidity.
